title: Write Address (AW) Handshake Violation
description: Crossbar deasserts AWREADY before the Master deasserts AWVALID, violating the AXI-Lite handshake rule that READY must hold until VALID is sampled.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [AXI_PROT_CHECK] AWREADY dropped before AWVALID handshake complete
expected_root_cause: The AW-channel READY logic is combinationally gated by an internal stall signal without a registered hold, causing READY to glitch low mid-handshake [1].
failure_log:
T=20ns: AWVALID=1, AWREADY=1
T=25ns: AWREADY=0 (premature)
UVM_ERROR: READY dropped mid-handshake.
success_log: AWREADY remains stable high until posedge clk samples AWVALID.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin if (!rst_n) awready <= 0; else awready <= !internal_stall; end

title: Write Data (W) Valid Without Address Phase
description: The Master sends WVALID before AWVALID, but the crossbar does not buffer the write data, causing data to be silently dropped.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_DATA] WDATA received with no pending AWADDR — data dropped
expected_root_cause: The crossbar lacks a write-data buffer for out-of-order W/AW arrival; it expects strict AW-before-W ordering not required by AXI-Lite [1, 2].
failure_log:
T=10: WVALID=1, AWVALID=0. Crossbar discarded WDATA.
UVM_ERROR: Scoreboard mismatch — data not written.
success_log: Crossbar buffers WDATA until AWADDR arrives and issues combined write.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin if (wvalid) wdata_buf <= wdata; if (awvalid && w_buf_valid) do_write <= 1; end

title: Read Data Channel RDATA X-State Propagation
description: The crossbar drives RDATA from an uninitialized register on the first read after reset, propagating X values to the master.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SVA_XZ] RDATA contains unknown bits while RVALID is high
expected_root_cause: The read data register is not initialized in the reset branch of its always_ff block, leaving it in state X on first access [3].
failure_log:
T=30: rst_n=1. T=40: RVALID=1, RDATA=32'hXXXXXXXX.
UVM_ERROR: X-propagation on read path.
success_log: RDATA is 32'h0 after reset; valid data on subsequent reads.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) if (!rst_n) rdata <= 32'h0; else rdata <= mem[addr];
testbench: initial begin rst_n=0; #20; rst_n=1; drive_read(); end

title: Write Strobe Zero Causes Silent No-Op
description: When WSTRB=4'b0000, the crossbar executes a write to the slave without any byte enables, writing nothing but generating a successful BRESP, masking a missing strobe error.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_DATA] WSTRB=0 accepted; no data written but BVALID asserted
expected_root_cause: The WSTRB validity check is absent; the protocol requires at least one strobe bit to be set for a valid write transfer [1, 4].
failure_log:
WSTRB=4'b0000, WVALID=1. BRESP=OKAY. RAM unchanged.
UVM_ERROR: Illegal no-op write accepted.
success_log: WSTRB=0 generates SLVERR or is rejected before write occurs.
rtl: always_ff @(posedge clk) if (wvalid && wready) mem[addr] <= wdata;
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) if (wvalid && wready && |wstrb) begin foreach(wstrb[i]) if (wstrb[i]) mem[addr][i*8+:8] <= wdata[i*8+:8]; end

title: DECERR Response Not Generated for Unmapped Address
description: Accesses to the unmapped range 0xF000–0xFFFF hang indefinitely because the crossbar has no error slave and no timeout mechanism.
bug_signature: UVM_FATAL: [TIMEOUT] No ARREADY/AWREADY for 10000 cycles at addr 0xF000
expected_root_cause: The address decoder case statement has no default branch to route unmapped addresses to a DECERR generator [5, 6].
failure_log: ADDR=0xF800. No slave selected. READY never asserted. Simulation timeout.
success_log: ADDR=0xF800 -> DECERR (RRESP=2'b11) returned within 2 cycles.
fix_replacement: unique case(addr[15:12]) 4'h0: sel_s0=1; 4'h1: sel_s1=1; default: sel_err=1; endcase

title: Simultaneous AWVALID and ARVALID Arbitration Deadlock
description: When both AWVALID and ARVALID are asserted simultaneously, the internal arbiter grants neither, entering a deadlock state.
bug_signature: UVM_FATAL: [DEADLOCK] AWVALID=1 and ARVALID=1 both stuck — neither granted after 5000 cycles
expected_root_cause: The arbitration condition uses XOR logic (`arvalid ^ awvalid`) which evaluates to 0 when both are high, preventing any grant [7, 8].
failure_log: ARVALID=1, AWVALID=1. GNT_AR=0, GNT_AW=0. Simulation timeout at 5000 cycles.
success_log: Read granted first; write follows after read completes.
rtl: assign gnt_ar = arvalid ^ awvalid; assign gnt_aw = awvalid ^ arvalid;
fix_replacement: assign gnt_ar = arvalid; assign gnt_aw = !arvalid && awvalid;
testbench: task run(); fork drive_read(); drive_write(); join endtask

title: BVALID Held High After BREADY Handshake
description: After a successful B-channel handshake (BVALID=1 && BREADY=1), BVALID is not cleared, causing the master to misinterpret the next cycle as a second write response.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [AXI_PROT_CHECK] Duplicate BVALID detected — no new write in progress
expected_root_cause: The BVALID clear logic is missing its enable condition; it only sets BVALID but never clears it after the handshake [1, 9].
failure_log:
T=100: BVALID=1, BREADY=1 (handshake OK)
T=110: BVALID=1 (stuck)
UVM_ERROR: Spurious BVALID.
success_log: BVALID cleared on posedge clk following BREADY handshake.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin if (!rst_n) bvalid <= 0; else if (wr_done) bvalid <= 1; else if (bvalid && bready) bvalid <= 0; end
testbench: task run(); drive_write(); @(posedge clk iff bvalid && bready); @(posedge clk); assert(bvalid == 0); endtask

title: Read Address Not Latched — Address Changes During Handshake
description: The crossbar uses ARADDR combinationally to drive the slave select without latching it, so if the master changes ARADDR before ARREADY, the wrong slave is accessed.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_MISMATCH] Read response from S1 for address targeting S0
expected_root_cause: ARADDR is used directly in combinational decoding without being registered at the ARVALID/ARREADY handshake point [1, 10].
failure_log: T=10: ARADDR=0x1000 (S0). T=15: ARADDR=0x2000 (S1, changed). T=20: ARREADY=1. Slave S1 accessed instead of S0.
success_log: ARADDR latched on handshake; downstream decoding uses registered value.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) if (arvalid && arready) lat_araddr <= araddr; assign slave_sel = decode(lat_araddr);
testbench: task run(); vif.arvalid <= 1; vif.araddr <= 16'h1000; #5; vif.araddr <= 16'h2000; @(posedge clk); endtask

title: RVALID Asserted Without Corresponding Read Request
description: The crossbar spontaneously asserts RVALID with stale RDATA from a previous transaction when no ARVALID has been seen.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [AXI_PROT_CHECK] RVALID high with no pending ARVALID transaction
expected_root_cause: The read pipeline state machine transitions to the RVALID state on a combinational signal that glitches without a valid AR-channel handshake [11].
failure_log:
T=50: ARVALID=0, RVALID=1, RDATA=0xDEAD. No request pending.
UVM_ERROR: Spurious read response.
success_log: RVALID asserted only after AR-channel handshake registers an outstanding read.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) if (!rst_n) rvalid <= 0; else if (ar_done) rvalid <= 1; else if (rvalid && rready) rvalid <= 0;

title: AWPROT Bits Ignored — Secure/Non-Secure Bypass
description: The crossbar routes all transactions to protected slave registers regardless of the AWPROT[1] (Non-Secure) bit, bypassing security isolation.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [PROT_FAIL] Non-secure write (AWPROT=2'b10) reached secure slave S2
expected_root_cause: The secure slave selection logic does not check AWPROT[1], allowing non-secure masters to access secure registers [12, 13].
failure_log:
AWPROT=3'b010 (Non-Secure). Secure slave S2 accessed. SLVERR not generated.
UVM_ERROR: Security violation.
success_log: AWPROT[1]=1 required for S2 access; non-secure transactions get DECERR.
fix_replacement: assign sel_s2 = (addr[15:12] == 4'hF) && (awprot[1] == 1'b0);

title: Byte Enable Misalignment on 16-bit Slave
description: A 16-bit aligned write with WSTRB=4'b0011 is routed to a 16-bit slave but the strobe bits are not remapped, causing the upper byte to be written instead of the lower.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_DATA] Byte 1 written to offset 0; Byte 0 not written
expected_root_cause: Strobe remapping for sub-word slave widths is missing; the lower 2 bits of WSTRB must be selected for a 16-bit lower-half transfer [14, 15].
failure_log:
Master WSTRB=4'b0011. Slave_WSTRB=4'b0011 (unremapped for 16-bit).
UVM_ERROR: Upper byte written instead of lower.
success_log: WSTRB correctly remapped for 16-bit slave interface.
fix_replacement: assign s_wstrb = (addr[1]) ? wstrb[3:2] : wstrb[1:0];

title: FSM One-Hot Encoding Fault in Crossbar State Machine
description: The crossbar transaction FSM uses one-hot encoding but the synthesis tool infers a binary encoder, causing illegal state combinations on power-up.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [FSM_STATE] Multiple one-hot bits active simultaneously: state=3'b011
expected_root_cause: The FSM state register is missing the `(* fsm_encoding = "one_hot" *)` synthesis attribute, defaulting to auto-encoding which may choose binary [16].
failure_log:
Post-synthesis simulation: state=3'b011 at T=0 (power-up).
UVM_ERROR: Illegal one-hot state.
success_log: FSM in IDLE (3'b001) immediately after reset.
fix_replacement: (* fsm_encoding = "one_hot" *) reg [2:0] state;
testbench: initial begin rst_n=0; #10; rst_n=1; @(posedge clk); assert($onehot(state)); end

title: Outstanding Transaction Counter Overflow
description: The crossbar allows more than the maximum outstanding transactions (N=4) because the counter uses a 2-bit register that wraps from 3 to 0 silently.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [OVERFLOW] Outstanding count exceeded max=4; accepting 5th transaction
expected_root_cause: The 2-bit counter (max value 3) wraps around to 0 when 4 transactions are outstanding, making it appear empty rather than full [17].
failure_log:
COUNT=3 (binary 11). Increment: COUNT=0 (wrap). AWREADY=1 (incorrectly).
UVM_ERROR: 5th transaction accepted.
success_log: AWREADY=0 when count reaches MAX_OUTSTANDING=4.
fix_replacement: reg [2:0] count; // 0-7, compare against MAX_OUTSTANDING=4

title: Unregistered Combinational Loop in READY Logic
description: AWREADY is driven by a combinational path that includes AWREADY itself as an input, creating a zero-delay combinational loop that causes simulation oscillation.
bug_signature: VCS-ERROR: Combinational loop detected involving net 'awready'
expected_root_cause: The READY generation logic creates a feedback path: `awready = !busy && awready` — a self-referential combinational expression [18].
failure_log:
Elaboration error: combinational loop. Simulation delta-cycle oscillation.
VCS-ERROR: awready undefined.
success_log: awready updated on posedge clk only — no loop.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) if (!rst_n) awready <= 0; else awready <= !busy;

title: RRESP SLVERR Incorrectly Returned for Valid Read
description: All read responses carry RRESP=2'b10 (SLVERR) regardless of whether the address is valid, causing the master to abort all read transactions.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_MISMATCH] Expected RRESP=OKAY (0), Got SLVERR (2) for valid address 0x0100
expected_root_cause: The RRESP mux has its inputs swapped; SLVERR is wired where OKAY should be [19].
failure_log:
ADDR=0x0100 (valid, mapped to S0). RRESP=2'b10.
Master aborted transaction.
UVM_ERROR: Unexpected SLVERR.
success_log: RRESP=2'b00 for valid addresses; 2'b10 only for unmapped addresses.
fix_replacement: assign rresp = (valid_addr) ? 2'b00 : 2'b10;

title: Write Channel Back-Pressure Not Applied to Master
description: The crossbar continues accepting write data (WREADY=1) even when the internal write queue is full, causing data to be silently overwritten.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [SBD_DATA] Write queue overflow; transaction at 0x2000 overwrote 0x1000 data
expected_root_cause: WREADY is hardwired to 1 instead of being gated by the write queue's full status [20].
failure_log:
WR_QUEUE_FULL=1. WREADY=1 (incorrect). 5th write accepted — overwrote entry 0.
UVM_ERROR: Data corruption.
success_log: WREADY=0 when write queue is full; master waits.
fix_replacement: assign wready = !wr_queue_full;

title: SVA Liveness Property Missing — Deadlock Undetected
description: The testbench has only safety assertions (no illegal states), but lacks a liveness assertion that ARREADY must eventually be asserted after ARVALID, allowing a deadlock to go undetected.
bug_signature: UVM_INFO: All safety assertions passed. Simulation completed. (ARREADY never asserted — missed by lack of liveness check)
expected_root_cause: Verification gap: no `eventually` or bounded-liveness SVA to ensure ARREADY responds within N cycles of ARVALID [21, 22].
failure_log:
ARVALID=1 for 10000 cycles. ARREADY never seen. Test PASSED (no liveness check).
UVM_ERROR (after adding assertion): Liveness violation.
success_log: Assertion fires within 16 cycles of ARVALID asserting.
fix_replacement: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) arvalid |-> ##[1:16] arready);
testbench: initial assert property (@(posedge clk) arvalid |-> ##[1:16] arready);

title: UVM Scoreboard Write Port Not Connected
description: The UVM monitor's analysis port is not connected to the scoreboard's write export, causing the scoreboard to see zero transactions and report false coverage.
bug_signature: UVM_WARNING: [SBD_IDLE] Scoreboard received 0 transactions after 10000 cycles
expected_root_cause: Missing `connect_phase` wiring between the monitor's `ap` (analysis port) and the scoreboard's `analysis_export` [23, 24].
failure_log:
10000 cycles completed. SBD transaction count=0.
UVM_WARNING: Scoreboard is idle — likely wiring error.
success_log: Scoreboard receives transactions for every AXI-Lite transfer and reports matching counts.
fix_replacement: function void connect_phase(uvm_phase phase); mon.ap.connect(sb.analysis_export); endfunction
testbench: function void connect_phase(uvm_phase phase); /* missing connect */ endfunction

title: Address Phase Accepted Without VALID — Protocol Violation
description: The crossbar samples AWADDR on a rising edge even when AWVALID is low, latching garbage data as a pending write address.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [AXI_PROT_CHECK] Address latched while AWVALID=0
expected_root_cause: The address latch enable condition incorrectly uses `awready` alone instead of `awvalid && awready` [1, 25].
failure_log:
T=10: AWVALID=0, AWREADY=1. AWADDR=0xDEAD (floating). lat_addr=0xDEAD.
UVM_ERROR: Invalid address accepted.
success_log: Address only latched when both AWVALID and AWREADY are high.
fix_replacement: always_ff @(posedge clk) if (awvalid && awready) lat_addr <= awaddr;
testbench: task run(); vif.awvalid <= 0; vif.awready <= 1; @(posedge clk); endtask

title: Slave Timeout Register Not Accessible via Crossbar
description: A configuration register at 0x0FF0 (slave timeout control) is never accessible because the crossbar's upper address bound check uses a strict less-than instead of less-than-or-equal.
bug_signature: UVM_ERROR: [DECERR] Address 0x0FF0 generated DECERR but is in the valid S0 range
expected_root_cause: The boundary check `addr < 16'h1000` excludes address 0x0FF0 from the valid S0 range when it should be included [5, 26].
failure_log:
ADDR=0x0FF0. Crossbar check: 0x0FF0 < 0x1000 = True (should be selected). ERROR: Route sent to DECERR.
UVM_ERROR: Off-by-one in boundary check.
success_log: 0x0FF0 routes to S0; register accessible and returns correct value.
fix_replacement: assign sel_s0 = (addr >= 16'h0000) && (addr <= 16'h0FFF);
